function: LEO satellite beam management: GRNN predicts the next beam cell for the CSI-RS search set; Twin DQN decides when to trigger beam tracking (pp. 1, 5).
system: LEO satellite with 49x49 uniform planar array, 547-beam codebook, user receives a scalar signal (eq. 7), 11.45 GHz carrier, no RIS (pp. 3, 10-11).
method: GRNN (60 parameters) trained with supervised first-order meta-learning; Twin DQN (deep reinforcement learning) trained with meta-learning; zero-shot testing without fine-tuning (pp. 6, 10, 13).
data_channel: Custom simulator: free-space path loss plus Rician fading (KR=10 dB), Starlink-like LEO geometry, random-walk user mobility, 1000 trajectories per reference angle; no public dataset (pp. 3, 11).
test_conditions: Train on antenna reference angles (integers in 0-180 degrees; 10 random angles for Twin DQN); test on different unseen angles, zero-shot, no fine-tuning (pp. 11, 13).
baselines: GRU (beam prediction); Double DQN; non-learned Benchmark 1 (CSI-RS to six neighbors) and Benchmark 2 (sweep when SNR below 2.5 dB) (pp. 11, 13).
metrics: Beam prediction accuracy, average reward as data rate (bits/s/Hz), SNR against optimal-beam upper bound, share of resources used by CSI-RS (pp. 12-14).
complexity: GRNN has 3K=60 parameters versus 32,850 for GRU; storage O(3K), compute O(NC^2); inference 4.98 ms (GRNN) and 23.8 ms (Twin DQN) on CPU (pp. 7, 8, 11, 14).
q1_support: p. 11: "The small-scale fading follows the Rician fading model with KR = 10 dB". Custom simulator (free-space path loss, p. 3, plus Rician fading); no 3GPP, QuaDRiGa, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data is used.
q2_support: p. 13: "The reference angles are different from that in meta-training and meta-validation sets, and we do not have data samples in these unseen scenarios."
q3_support: p. 13: "Compared with the straightforward application of Double DQN" (learned baseline); p. 14: "the two benchmarks without machine learning, the proposed method can achieve more than 20% performance gain" (non-learned baselines).
q4_support: p. 14: "The average processing time of GRNN is 4.98 ms, and the average processing time of Twin DQN is 23.8 ms"; p. 7: "The storage requirement is O(3K)".
q5_support: p. 11: "In our simulation, the mobility of the satellite, the rotation of the earth, and the random mobility of the user are considered". Data come from the authors' own simulator; the paper gives no code or data link and uses no public dataset.
notes: Included, area 6: the learned methods control the beams of an LEO satellite link (p. 1). The satellite has a 49x49 array, so the single-antenna check does not apply. Test reference angles are disjoint from training and validation (Tables I-II, p. 11). Conference version is cited as [1].
